core_obligations: Lift the augmentation to phi: R[x] -> A(0); pick xi_j with d(xi_j) = phi(f_j) using H_0(A) = S.
Compute d(sum phi(r_j) xi_j) = 0; since H_1(A) = 0 pick xi in A_2 with d(xi) = sum phi(r_j) xi_j; coefficients of r_j in I make xi a class in H_2(A/IA).
Lift everything to the A'(i): phi', xi'_j with d(xi'_j) = phi'(f'_j) + f a_j, and a lift xi' with d(xi') = sum phi'(r'_j) xi'_j + sum f b_i T_i.
Apply d once more: theta(xi) = sum phi'(r'_j) phi'(f'_j) + two vanishing terms (coefficients in I are annihilated by f; d(T_i) maps to zero in H_0); read off theta(xi) = g.
proof_roadmap: Execute the two-stage computation in the Tate filtration and account for all three terms of the final application of d.
difficulty_reason: Explicit term-by-term computation; every displayed identity must be traced through the filtration.
